name: Plutocracy
summary: Plutocracy is a society ruled or controlled by people of great wealth, a kind of oligarchy in which the ruling few are rich. The term is used by critics to describe or warn against such a condition; the reference sources note that governments and organisations do not label themselves plutocracies and that it is not rooted in an established political philosophy, so no body of positions of its own is recorded.
scope: Plutocracy as defined by the reference works that name it: rule by or control of government by the very wealthy, whether formal or through influence over a nominal democracy. No programme, school or thinker is presented by those sources as plutocracy's own, so critics' accounts (Theodore Roosevelt's attack on the tyranny of a plutocracy, Krugman, Stiglitz, Chomsky) and the positions of oligarchy, elitism, corporatocracy or capitalism are not counted as plutocracy's positions.
